concept: A monumental female figure in profile, half-submerged in shadow and half-illuminated, holding aloft a delicate circuit board or mathematical formula that glows with soft light. Behind her, fragmented architectural forms—a courtroom, a prison wall, an apartment doorway, a space capsule—all crumbling or dissolving into smoke. Her face is serene and forward-gazing despite the chaos. Bold, geometric shadows dominate the lower half; the upper half transitions to ethereal light. Style: dystopian realism meets Soviet constructivism, high contrast, monumental scale.
explanation: Today's news spans profound contrasts: the death of Margaret Hamilton, a visionary whose work lifted humanity toward the stars, juxtaposed against a cascade of stories about injustice, torture, compromise, and collective failure to hold power accountable. I chose to honor Hamilton's legacy—a woman who proved that intellectual courage and moral clarity can move mountains—while surrounding her with the fractured institutions and moral ambiguities that dominate the rest of the day's headlines. The glow she holds represents hope and human achievement; the shadows represent the institutional rot, political cowardice, and unresolved violence that define most of today's news.

headlines.title: US and Lebanon protecting wanted Syrian general, BBC finds
headlines.summary: Bassam al-Hassan, linked to reporter Austin Tice's abduction, is being sheltered in return for information.

headlines.title: Texas carries out first US execution since Christa Pike's botched lethal injections
headlines.summary: Lawyers for Jamaal Howard had asked a judge to pause the execution after Christa Pike's botched lethal injections.

headlines.title: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies
headlines.summary: Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years in September.

headlines.title: Margaret Hamilton, whose software helped land Apollo 11 on the Moon, dies at 90
headlines.summary: Pioneering computer scientist led the development of the software for Nasa's Apollo mission and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

headlines.title: France's school protests: What lies behind the anger
headlines.summary: Students' blockades and marches spring from real grievances – and from France's habit of settling policy on the street.

headlines.title: New York court hears arguments in ongoing 9/11 families' lawsuit against Saudi Arabia
headlines.summary: The families allege that men with links to the Saudi government helped those who carried out the 2001 attacks, something the country denies.

headlines.title: Trump wants a new Camp David-like retreat at his Florida golf club
headlines.summary: Trump's estate would stand in stark contrast to the rustic Camp David and mark another tradition transformed by Trump.

headlines.title: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro expected to face more charges this week
headlines.summary: The new charges are expected to accuse Maduro and his wife of playing a role in the torture of Americans in Venezuelan prisons, US media reports.

headlines.title: Japan beer giants raided over alleged price-fixing cartel
headlines.summary: Asahi, Sapporo, Kirin and Suntory confirmed to the BBC that their premises had been searched by the Japanese competition authority.

headlines.title: Three people killed in Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia airports, officials say
headlines.summary: The Houthis have claimed responsibility for the attacks, which mark an escalation in the conflict.

headlines.title: Veteran Indian actor Nana Patekar dies at 75
headlines.summary: Known for his intense performances, Patekar carved out a distinctive place in Indian cinema.

headlines.title: Israelis demand accountability over 7 October failures three years after attacks
headlines.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has refused to take any personal responsibility for what happened or order a state inquiry.
